rationale: read_text_file takes character indices, not line numbers: it slices content[offset:end_idx] with end_idx = min(offset + limit, total_chars), sets has_more = end_idx < total_chars, and returns next_offset = end_idx when more remains. task: The Hindi monologue at sample_data/demo2_hindi_spoken_monologue.ogg has to become an English transcript for the blog. Give me the English wording directly instead of Hindi text I would have to convert in a second pass.
rationale: The task parameter is typed Literal['transcribe','translate'], and 'translate' is the documented direct-to-English path, so a single speech call satisfies the request; leaving task at its 'transcribe' default would return Hindi and force a second translate_text pass. The file is 3.5 minutes, and transcribe_audio slices anything over 30 s internally with max_chunk_sec=28.0 before joining the chunk results, so no chunk_audio step is needed. language='hi' is checked against SUPPORTED_INDIC_LANGS and forwarded as data['language'], so the known language is pinned rather than auto-detected.

task: Same intake recording, sample_data/demo2_hindi_spoken_monologue.ogg, but this time I need the exact Hindi words for a verbatim quote. The speaker is definitely Hindi, so pin the language down instead of leaving it to auto-detection.
rationale: task defaults to 'transcribe' and the Literal type accepts only 'transcribe' or 'translate'; 'transcribe' returns the spoken language verbatim, whereas 'translate' would return English and break the quotation requirement. language='hi' is a member of SUPPORTED_INDIC_LANGS, so it passes the guard and reaches _call_transcribe as data['language'], eliminating the model's language guess on a known Hindi file. The 3.5-minute duration is handled internally at 28 s silence boundaries, so chunk_audio is not a prerequisite and no max_chunk_sec argument exists on this tool.

task: The IndicNLP paper at sample_data/demo1_indic_nlp_paper.pdf is 14 pages, and its appendices begin on page 6. Pull the text from pages 1 to 5 only and stop there; no appendix page should be processed or billed.
rationale: page_limit is a count, not a page range: extract_document_text forwards it to rasterize_document_pages(path, tmp_dir, dpi=150, page_limit=page_limit), which renders the first page_limit pages and stops. On a 14-page PDF, page_limit=5 is exactly 'pages 1 to 5', so pages 6-14 are never rasterized or sent to indic-ocr; leaving it None would bill all 14 pages. There is no start-page argument to set, and table_format can stay at its 'markdown' default because no HTML is requested.

task: Our CMS rejects pipe tables, so the Marathi worksheet image sample_data/demo3_marathi_devanagari_table.png has to come out as real HTML table markup with <tr> and <td> cells that I can paste into the editor.
rationale: table_format is a Literal['markdown','html'] that extract_document_text interpolates into the OCR instruction 'Format tables as {table_format}.', so 'html' is what makes indic-ocr emit <tr>/<td> markup; the 'markdown' default would emit pipe characters the CMS rejects. A .png bypasses rasterize_document_pages and goes straight to _ocr_images([path]), so page_limit has no effect on an image and must not be invented. inspect_media only returns size_bytes and format and can never read the cell contents.

task: Quick check before I file this note: is धन्यवाद। Hindi or Marathi, and which script is it written in? Tell me what the characters alone can prove.
rationale: The string holds eight code points in U+0900-U+097F (danda included), so detect_language returns script 'Devanagari' with likely_languages ['hi','mr','sa','ne','kok','mai','bho','doi'] and confidence 'medium', because the 'high' branch requires char_count > 10. It therefore cannot settle Hindi versus Marathi, and the honest reply is that candidate list rather than a paid translate_text call or a guess. The value belongs in text; detect_language takes no file path, and truncating or stripping the danda would not change the candidate set.
